pr_body:
Implements the CAP acceptor role

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41711

This PR contains a needed improvement for TBS, but that can be moved out to a separate PR if wanted by reviewers.
pr_comments: @asbjornsabo Some commits seems to have messed up a few things - I'll do a commit-per-commit review myself and fix them :)

> I recall this code failed to build for me when TBS/CCP was disabled. Maybe you fixed this already, I used one of the previous versions

Yes, that was fixed (and caught by the testcase added by you :) )
@asbjornsabo @MariuszSkamra @Casper-Bonde-Bose I've added a new commit that moved the metadata type verification to the application instead.

> @Thalley I suggest that you raise an erratum to get some working group discussion on the question on rejecting RFU metadata.

I disagree. I believe this is an implementation detail. In the end, it will be the application that needs to be qualified, so that test case will be up to the application.
Rebased to solve merge conflicts and resolve https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/44522#discussion_r914494400

issue_context.title: LE Audio: CAP Acceptor Implementation
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Implement the CAP Acceptor role (https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/specs/common-audio-profile/) and Service (https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/specs/common-audio-service/).

review_comments:
I am not sure this function does what it's expected to do. It's named `bt_cap_acceptor_register` which implies that it will register CAP profile role, but it does it's registration on GATT CAS instance.
I guess that it's insufficient. Is it really needed to have a such function? Why the CAS could not be registered if some Kconfig option e.g. `BT_AUDIO_ROLE_ACCEPTOR` is set?

The CAP specification says:
```
An Acceptor:
• Can transmit and receive unicast Audio Streams
• Can expose Audio Stream Endpoints (ASEs)
• Can receive broadcast Audio Streams
• Signals availability and support for different use cases as described by Context Type values
• Receives context on the intended use case of unicast or broadcast Audio Streams as described by
Context Type values
• Receives information on the association of unicast or broadcast Audio Streams with Content Control
services through CCID values
• Can scan for broadcast Audio Streams
• Can delegate scanning for broadcast Audio Streams to a Commander
• Can request and receive a Broadcast_Code
• Can receive requests from a Commander to start or stop reception of broadcast Audio Streams
• Can receive requests from a Commander to mute and set the volume of audio that the Acceptor is
rendering
• Can receive requests from a Commander to mute and set the signal level of its microphone
• Can host CCP and MCP clients
```

This response is also for https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/44522#discussion_r864527215:

Basically I would have liked to do static allocation only. This is still possible, but the CSIS is dynamically registered and require a set of parameters to be registered. I ended up with this dynamic allocation for CAS with CSIS, such that the upper layer can provide those parameters to the CAS CSIS instance. 
It would be possible to add Kconfig options for the parameters for the CAS CSIS instance, and that way make it statically registered, even when the CAP Acceptor is a set member. 

Regarding the name (if we keep it as dynamic), we can rename it to `bt_cap_csis_register` or `bt_cap_acceptor_register_csis` (to keep the profile role as the function prefix) if that is better (if we add Kconfigs for the CSIS parameters and always statically register CAS, then this function goes away)

Maybe nothing to-do, but a comment on this comment, I have noticed clients that does send the CCID list seemingly based only on supporting conversational context, even when TBS or MCS is not supported
It does not make any sense to put a CCID if TBS or MCS is not supported. CCID is used to identify a TBS or MCS instance. The CCID has no context or value outside of that.
I'm in full agreement with you :)

Should this be CONFIG_BT_CAS?  If not - what is the purpose of the CONFIG_BT_CAS?
(Maybe the answer will become clear in the next commit.)
Removed `CONFIG_BT_CAS` as it held no value
Would be good to have at least short doxygen documentation of those values, what are those, where they come from etc.
Why `CONFIG_BT_CAP_ACCEPTOR_SET_MEMBER` implies GATT service dynamic registration?
I am certain this will cause problems just like *unsupported* metadata type. Does the spec mandates the maximum number of metadata fields? Why not to parse *known* specific metadata types only?

> Why not to parse known specific metadata types only?

You mean truncate the metadata to fit the memory allocated in Zephyr?

I guess we can do that, but in the case of e.g. CAP (which mandates e.g. the streaming context metadata), then we may end up truncating required metadata. 

Perhaps ideally the stack wouldn't need to store this data, and probably just provide the metadata as a `bt_data` to the upper layers as is, which I guess is similar to what is being requested in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/42860
So why not to parse and store required metadata only?

> So why not to parse and store required metadata only?

We could/should do that, but that seems outside the scope of this PR, as that is changing how we store metadata (and then we need to refactor all metadata handling in ASCS). 

I suggest to postpone this to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/42860

Ditto. This might cause potential issues sooner or later. I would recommend to check *known* fields only, and just live with that the field can be shortened (e.g. name of TV Station) to fit the CONFIG_BT_CODEC_MAX_METADATA_LEN
The problem is that we store the metadata in the stack at the moment, so even the known metadata field may not fit into the allocated memory.
